A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Forecasting Company Fundamentals and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Their shared experiments and retained material can be reliably matched despite added content and changed pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting evaluations, simulated investment returns, dataset analyses, and RevIN and human-forecast comparisons in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations of xLSTM-Mixer and Chronos configurations, together with quantitative static-feature ablation results.

M1.justification: The domain-specific normalization and forecasting/backtesting procedures are retained. xLSTM-Mixer and Chronos are additional existing comparison methods; their inclusion does not establish a change to a proposed algorithm. The expanded cleaning description documents the existing 19-company exclusion.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same reported 2,527-company dataset spanning 2009 Q1–2023 Q3, with 20 indicators and five prediction targets. The StarMine human-forecast coverage and investment scenarios are retained. No additional evaluation dataset or domain is introduced.

E2.justification: v2 adds xLSTM-Mixer and Chronos Small/Base to the main benchmark and human-forecast comparison, in Table 2 and the renumbered Table 7. The existing comparators remain, and the investment comparison methods are unchanged.

E3.justification: The added comparisons include two pretrained configurations, Chronos Bolt Small and Bolt Base. The retained experiments keep the 40 expanding-window folds, twelve-quarter lookback, four-quarter horizon, 10% company validation holdout, metrics, and portfolio design. No rerun of the retained experiments is established.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.5 and Table 6 quantify the effect of supplying GICS static features for five models, supporting a previously qualitative claim. NLinear changes from 0.136 to 0.135 nCRPS, while TFT changes from 0.132 to 0.134. Existing feature, time, and horizon analyses also include additional models; the RevIN ablation is retained.

E5.justification: The new xLSTM-Mixer and Chronos rows omit standard deviations for RSE and R² in Tables 2 and 7, unlike the retained rows. Otherwise, the existing mean/standard-deviation reporting and statistical tests remain; no new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds numerical results and curves for three model configurations and the static-feature ablation, including xLSTM-Mixer's reported 0.141 nCRPS in Table 7. All retained main-benchmark, human-comparison, and RevIN table entries are unchanged, as are the investment returns. Some new Table 2 values conflict with Figure 1.

T1.justification: The mathematical model descriptions and metric formulas are retained. The RevIN equation is reformatted without changing its substance. The added model descriptions introduce no new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion expand the stated comparison from 22 to 24 models. The central claims about probabilistic deep-learning forecasts, comparison with human analysts, investment utility, and opportunities for expert involvement otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 suggests that short time series explain Chronos's difficulties and that overfitting could explain TFT's deterioration with static features. It also adds future directions involving data upsampling and company-specific analysis. The existing interpretations of pandemic effects, seasonality, and investment limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Section 4.1.2 specifies the two-round, 30-standard-deviation cleaning rule behind the retained exclusions. Appendix A.3 newly provides an implementation-access statement and code/source links. The human comparison is explicitly identified as using probabilistic models; most previously documented hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion covering xLSTM-Mixer, Chronos, mixing architectures, and pretraining, and explicitly connects the retained recurrent models to DeepAR. Additional citations support upsampling and interpretability discussion. The paper's overall positioning as a comparative company-fundamentals study remains stable.

P1.justification: There are targeted grammar, terminology, affiliation, and explanatory edits, plus new model-description paragraphs and a static-feature appendix subsection. The six main sections retain their organization. The human-comparison appendix moves from A.5 to A.6 rather than being replaced.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 gain model-family labels and additional bars; Figures 4–6 incorporate additional models and updated labels or legends. Existing comparison tables gain rows, and a new static-feature table is inserted. Captions and float placement change within the same overall document layout.

improvement.justification: The added comparators, quantified static-feature analysis, cleaning details, and code-access information are useful. However, the new benchmark evidence is internally inconsistent: Table 2 reports Chronos Small sMAPE of 0.421 versus ARMean(1)'s 0.482, while Figure 1 places Chronos near 0.60 and the text still identifies ARMean(1) as best. The PDFs do not resolve which results to trust, preventing a reliable assessment of whether the additions outweigh the loss of reporting consistency.
